records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:51 — P2, confidence 100: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` changes an existing programmatic `ProcessSpansStrategyFactory(...)` call that omits the new option from one flusher to one spawned Sentry process and Kafka producer per assigned partition, while the CLI still supplies `default=1` at src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:434, so the same omitted configuration has two resource-allocation contracts and partition rebalances amplify process and connection counts for programmatic consumers; retain a shared default of one and require explicit opt-in for automatic per-shard expansion.
records.rationale: The finding correctly identifies a behavioral inconsistency. In the diff at line 51: `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`. When `max_processes` is None (not provided), this defaults to the number of assigned shards. However, the CLI option at line 434 sets `default=1`. This means: (1) CLI consumers get 1 flusher process by default, (2) Programmatic callers that don't pass `flusher_processes` get one process per shard. records.issue_text: src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:435 — P2, confidence 100: the new process-count option accepts nonpositive values through `type=int` without a lower-bound check, so configuring `--flusher-processes 0` with four assigned shards reaches `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and starts four workers despite the requested maximum, while `--flusher-processes -1` creates an empty shard map and raises `KeyError(0)` during startup; validate a positive count at the CLI and constructor boundaries to prevent an invalid deployment setting from silently expanding resource usage or stopping span ingestion.
